summary: Builds the unified per-building corner pool from upstream anchor sources: ridge-intersection corners, ridge-end corners, concave/convex anchors (from boundary-signals), and wall-bbox synthetic corners. Snaps remaining anchors onto nearby ridges, filters wrong-side convex anchors, then imports foreign-plane corners that fall on this plane (coplanar import). Emits a unified CORNERS section plus a new CORNER_MEMBERS section (per-corner pool-merge decomposition with source/authority/axis/ridge_id for boundary-regularize). Consumed downstream by boundary-polygons and boundary-merge.

phases.name: Wall-bbox corners
phases.description: For vertical planes only (tilt ≥ wall_tilt_min_deg), synthesizes corners at the plane's group bbox extents projected back into world space (gated by wall_min_h_extent on bbox width). Gives walls a deterministic polygon when signal-derived corners are too sparse.

phases.name: Ridge-intersection (RI) corner enrichment
phases.description: Pre-existing RI corners from boundary-topology get their planeIds, ridgeIds, dirsByPlane filled in by walking the ridges that meet at this corner.

phases.name: Ridge-end corners
phases.description: Ridges with no intersection coverage at one end get a synthetic 'ridge-end' corner emitted at that end's clamped t-value.

phases.name: Ridge snap
phases.description: For each unsnapped concave/convex anchor, finds the nearest ridge within snap_radius. If found, snaps the anchor onto the ridge's clamped t-projection, records ridgeId, marks anchor as snapped.

phases.name: Ridge-side filter (wrong-side kill)
phases.description: For each remaining unsnapped CONVEX anchor on plane g, tests against each ridge R of plane g: if perp distance to R's infinite line is ≤ ridge_side_max_dist AND the anchor is on the wrong side of R (opposite the plane interior, per RIDGE_LINES side_vec/side_sign), kill the anchor. Skipped on the anchor's snap-target ridge to avoid FP-sign-of-zero coin flips.

phases.name: Pool registration
phases.description: All surviving anchors (RI, ridge-end, concave, convex, wall-bbox) are inserted into the per-building corner pool via v7p_entry_register* — within pool_merge_dist of any existing member, higher-priority sources (v7p_src_priority: RI > ridge-end > polygon-merge > concave/convex > coplanar) absorb lower-priority entries; otherwise a new pool entry is opened. Each pool entry carries a per-plane source_per_plane[] parallel to plane_ids[].

phases.name: Coplanar import
phases.description: Scan the pool for foreign-plane corners that lie within coplanar_dist_threshold of this plane's equation AND have balance ≥ coplanar_balance_min on this plane's grid. Such corners get a 'coplanar' source label for this plane and are registered as members of this plane.

parameters.name: snap_radius
parameters.summary: Snap distance for concave/convex anchors to nearest ridge (D.2). Overridable via params JSON key snapRadius.
parameters.rationale: Loose enough to capture anchors near a ridge but not yet on it (typical detector noise is 5–20 cm); tight enough to avoid snapping across a different ridge of the same plane. Empirically tuned on dahouet.

parameters.name: wall_tilt_min_deg
parameters.summary: Minimum tilt-from-horizontal for a plane to be treated as a wall in D.0. Overridable via params JSON key wallTiltMinDeg.
parameters.rationale: 72° matches the wall classification threshold used by boundary-classify; below this, normals are too horizontal to qualify.

parameters.name: wall_side_margin
parameters.summary: Lateral inset for wall-bbox corners (D.0). Not overridable via params JSON in v3 (compile-time default only).
parameters.rationale: Walls' edges are rarely perfectly aligned with the group's bbox extremes; small inward inset avoids placing corners on noise.

parameters.name: wall_min_h_extent
parameters.summary: Minimum horizontal bbox width for a wall plane to emit D.0 corners. Not overridable via params JSON in v3.
parameters.rationale: Guard against degenerate vertical strips whose group bbox is too narrow to yield meaningful 4-corner geometry.

parameters.name: pool_merge_dist
parameters.summary: 3D radius within which a new anchor merges into an existing pool entry (D.3). Overridable via params JSON key poolMergeDist.
parameters.rationale: Slightly tighter than snap_radius so post-snap anchors that fell onto distinct ridge endpoints don't collapse together.

parameters.name: coplanar_dist_threshold
parameters.summary: Max perpendicular distance from foreign corner to this plane's equation for coplanar import (D.4). Overridable via params JSON key coplanarDistThreshold.
parameters.rationale: Tight: only corners physically on the plane should be imported. Loose values cause cross-plane corner pollution.

parameters.name: coplanar_balance_min
parameters.summary: Min balance-grid value at the foreign corner's projected location to qualify for coplanar import. Overridable via params JSON key coplanarBalanceMin.
parameters.rationale: Ensures the foreign corner sits in a *populated* region of this plane's grid, not on a sparse fringe.

parameters.name: ridge_side_max_dist
parameters.summary: Local-neighborhood radius for the ridge-side filter (D.2b). Overridable via params JSON key ridgeSideMaxDist.
parameters.rationale: Guard against courtyard-scale parallel ridges of the same plane — beyond this radius, two ridge-side relationships within a single plane are not meaningful constraints on each other. See related journal entry for the detailed design discussion; the value itself is a heuristic and the gate is under review.

history.note: Introduced at 0.6 m in boundary-3d's polygon optimization pipeline.
Widened to 1.5 m (commit not bisected — change happened during the boundary-3d → boundary-corners extraction).

parameters.name: up_axis
parameters.summary: World up axis: 1 = y-up (bench-parity mode), 2 = z-up (v3 prod default). Overridable via params JSON key upAxis.
parameters.rationale: v3 prod data is z-up; bench-v2 parity testing uses y-up like the JS pipeline. Selected per-pipeline by the wrapper default (z-up) or by params override.

reads.name: grm-owner
reads.description: Per-building Int16 owner array (which plane each building-point belongs to after grow-refit-merge).

reads.name: boundary-signals-roof-graph
reads.description: Per-building TLV — PLANES, RIDGES, RIDGE_LINES, CORNERS (RI seeds), PLANE_GRIDS (group + nearby + balance), NEARBY_PROJECTIONS, CONCAVE/CONVEX anchors.

writes.name: boundary-corners-roof-graph
writes.description: Per-building TLV (ARRAY_INLINE). CORNERS section (0x06) replaced by the unified pool — records carry: position, planeIds, ridgeIds, source_per_plane, name, n_merged, dirsByPlane, com_bisector_by_plane. NEW: CORNER_MEMBERS section (0x07) added — per-corner pool-merge decomposition (point, source, authority, axis, ridge_id at 48B/member) for boundary-regularize. All other upstream sections (PLANES, RIDGES, RIDGE_LINES, NEARBY_PROJECTIONS, PLANE_GRIDS) pass through unchanged.

v3_divergences.rationale: Per v7-boundary-corners-impl.h:51 — 'useMrAnchors is GONE — MR points are an edge slide signal for boundary-regularize, not corners; they're emitted by an upstream step that boundary-regularize will own.' v2's optional D.1c phase and useMrAnchors param are not ported. The v2 default was already off (6c4dd2c), so this is a removal of dead-by-default code.
Per v7-boundary-corners-impl.h:54 — handled in boundary-regularize. Not part of the v3 corner pool wire format.

v3_divergences.topic: CORNER_MEMBERS section (0x07) added as a new write
v3_divergences.rationale: v3 externalizes the pool-merge decomposition (point + source + authority + axis + ridge_id, 48B/member) into its own roof-graph section so boundary-regularize can re-derive per-anchor degrees of freedom without re-running pool merging. v2 kept this implicit in JS object refs.

v3_divergences.topic: PLANE_ANCHORS section dropped from upstream contract
v3_divergences.rationale: v2 boundary-signals emitted a separate PLANE_ANCHORS section; v3 folds anchors into the CORNERS section directly. Avoids a dead section in the wire format.

v3_divergences.topic: source_per_plane parallel array added to CORNERS
v3_divergences.rationale: The same pool entry needs different source labels for different planes (e.g., a corner that is 'convex' on plane 3 and 'coplanar' on plane 5). v2 had a single global source field; v3 makes it per-plane. Boundary-polygons reads per-plane source to honor priority correctly at init.

v3_divergences.topic: D.2b skips side test on snap-target ridge
v3_divergences.rationale: After snap, anchor sits *on* the ridge by construction so side_d is mathematically zero; FP rounding decides sign and randomly kills corners. Skip is a correctness fix, also backported to v2 (boundary-corners.js bumped 2 → 3).

related.summary: Comprehensive review of the wrong-side-corner-killing problem: two failure modes (segment range, courtyard parallel ridges), three candidate gates with pros/cons, U-shape counterexample, and the meta-critique that D.2b is treating an upstream symptom. Decision: keep current code aligned with v2 until v3 byte-parity is reached.
The roof-graph pre-pass that v7-boundary-corners + v7-boundary-polygons build on top of.
Root-cause fix for dahouet 7-shared-edges bug: v7-boundary-topology was emitting has_side=0 unconditionally, so every D.2b side test was silently skipped.
Add asserts on flag conditions at all RIDGE_LINES consumer sites to prevent future has_side-style silent-skip bugs.
Per-plane corner source — fixes coplanar-import label loss for corners that participate in multiple planes.
D.2b skip side test on the snap-target ridge — FP-sign-of-zero protection.
v2: extract Pass 1 + coplanar import from boundary-3d into the standalone boundary-corners step.
Wire format spec for the CORNERS section (including source_per_plane and dirsByPlane subrecords) and §4.7 CORNER_MEMBERS.
Port-level documentation: where v7-boundary-corners fits in the v3 v7 pipeline and what's still pending.

open_questions: Should D.2b's perpendicular-distance test use the ridge SEGMENT (clamped t) instead of the infinite line? (See journal 2026-05-17, failure mode 1.)
Should outward-direction (com_bisector_by_plane) be a third stacked gate on D.2b, on top of segment-distance + max-distance? (Has a known U-shape failure mode — see journal.)

Should D.2b exist at all? Could upstream changes (boundary-signals weighting by plane-interior consistency, more aggressive D.2 snap) make wrong-side anchors rare enough that the filter becomes unnecessary?
What is the false-positive rate of D.2b across the bench corpus (legitimate corners killed vs spurious convex anchors correctly killed)? Currently unmeasured.
